key_insight: VirTues-M2 jointly learns tissue morphology and spatial protein patterns to support multiple cancer research tasks within one model.
clinical_relevance: The model could help link routine H&E images with molecular tissue features for prognostic research, but clinical utility remains to be established.
method: Uses a multimodal vision transformer to integrate H&E histopathology and multiplex spatial proteomics.
Encodes marker identity to accommodate variable marker panels, missing modalities, and imperfect pairing or registration.
Supports tissue phenotyping, cell segmentation, virtual staining, biomarker discovery, and adaptive marker selection.
evidence_signal: In a newly collected cohort of 1,053 treatment-naive NSCLC patients with paired modalities, discovered tissue signatures stratified overall survival in discovery and independent validation cohorts, reportedly outperforming current state-of-the-art stratification schemes.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance estimates or prospective clinical evaluation, limiting assessment of effect size and deployment readiness.
paper_title: A multimodal foundation model for tissue proteomics and morphology in cancer
